title: Master list of official verified trusted sources
method: Each entry was verified line-by-line during the 2026-09-18 session: the URL was fetched or located via live search, and the 'verified' field records exactly what was observed. Nothing in this list is assumed.

sources.name: Kalshi (exchange, API & docs)
sources.type: Official exchange (CFTC-licensed DCM) + market data layer
sources.verified: Live public API queried 2026-09-18: GET /series, GET /markets (series_ticker filters PRES, CONTROLH, CONTROLS, SENATEAZ), GET /historical/cutoff, GET /historical/markets (settled 2024 markets with result=yes/no), GET /markets/{t}/candlesticks (daily history). Historical data docs page fetched: market_settled_ts partitioning confirmed.
sources.notes: Primary prediction-market data layer for this project.

sources.name: Federal Election Commission — Election Results
sources.type: Official government (results compiled from state election offices)
sources.verified: FEC page fetched via search (2026-09-18): 'Official 2024 Presidential General Election Results, compiled from state election offices (PDF)'; biennial 'Federal Elections' compilations described. 2024 results PDF cited by Wikipedia infobox: https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/2024presgeresults.pdf
sources.notes: Authoritative source for certified federal results (2020: 81,283,501 Biden / 74,223,975 Trump; 2024: 77,302,580 Trump / 75,017,613 Harris per the FEC PDF via Wikipedia infobox).

sources.name: U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC)
sources.verified: Verified via usa.gov agency page + Ballotpedia/Wikipedia (2026-09-18): federal commission created by HAVA 2002; develops voting system guidelines/certification.
sources.notes: FLAGGED: as of July 2026 the commission has no serving commissioners (two dismissed, one resigned) — irregularity #1; treat its guidance output accordingly until reconstituted.

sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau — CPS Voting & Registration Supplement
sources.verified: Census press release (2023-05-02) fetched via search: 2022 turnout 52.2% of CVAP, registration 69.1%; NBER-hosted raw files with DOI 10.60592/w6zf-md62 also located.
sources.notes: 2024 presidential turnout 64.3% (per University of Florida, cited in Wikipedia infobox) and 2020 turnout 66.6% (U.S. Elections Project, same infobox) — Census CPS is the comparable series.

sources.name: National Archives and Records Administration — Electoral College
sources.verified: FEC's election-results page (fetched 2026-09-18) designates NARA as the federal agency responsible for coordinating Electoral College functions between States and Congress.
sources.notes: Used for certified electoral vote tallies cross-checks.

sources.name: CQ Press — Voting & Elections Collection / CQ Congress
sources.verified: CQ 'Sources and Definitions' page fetched via search (2026-09-18): 'compiled from final, official results obtained from election authorities in each state'; district-level presidential votes computed from secretaries of state and boards of elections.
sources.notes: Institutional subscription database — use for research access where available.

sources.name: IFES Election Guide
sources.type: Nonprofit election research (International Foundation for Electoral Systems)
sources.verified: Election Guide 2024 US presidency page fetched via search: 'Results Source: Federal Election Commission, 2024presgeresults.pdf — Donald TRUMP won 312 electoral votes; Kamala HARRIS won 226 electoral votes'.

sources.name: Associated Press (AP News, AP VoteCast)
sources.verified: AP election result hubs fetched via search (2026-09-18); AP's 2020 certification article cited in Wikipedia 2020 infobox lead ('Biden officially secures enough electors to become president', 2020-12-05).

sources.name: Reuters
sources.verified: Reuters 2024 results page fetched via search (2026-09-18): state-by-state presidential calls (Trump wins WI/MI/GA/OK/KY/TN etc.), sourced from the National Election Pool (ABC, BBC, CBS, CNN).

sources.name: CNN (Election Center, CNN Poll of Polls)
sources.type: Official news outlet (results, forecasts, poll aggregations)
sources.verified: 2026-09-08 CNN midterm article fetched via search (Dems need 4 net Senate seats; core offensive map); CNN Poll of Polls referenced in CNN's Gallup-tracking story (2026-02-12): 39% approve / 59% disapprove avg of 134 polls.

sources.name: The New York Times
sources.verified: 2026-02-11 article fetched via search: 'Gallup Will No Longer Track Presidential Approval Ratings' (after nearly 90 years); last Gallup approval (Dec 2025): 36% approve.

sources.name: The Washington Post
sources.verified: 2026-06-23 analysis fetched via search: Post analyzed 2,000 primary markets on Kalshi/Polymarket — candidates priced ~75% won ~75% of the time; LA mayoral market passed $40M before voting ended (Spencer Pratt case).
sources.notes: Key external validation of prediction-market calibration.

sources.name: Gallup
sources.verified: Status verified via NYT (2026-02-11) and CNN (2026-02-12): Gallup ended presidential approval tracking (Feb 2026) and horse-race election polling (2015); longest-running continuous approval series since FDR. Final approval 36% (Dec 2025).
sources.notes: FLAGGED: no longer polls presidential approval/horse-race — historical series only (irregularity #4).

sources.name: Pew Research Center
sources.verified: 2026-09-16 report fetched via search: ~70% of 2024 national polls weighted on party/past-vote; political weighting 'modestly more accurate'. NPORS benchmark page: D+47/R+43/Refused 10 (Jan–Jun 2026).

sources.name: Quinnipiac University (Polling Institute)
sources.verified: 2026-09-10 release verified via syndication (masslive/pennlive/mlive, 2026-09-13): House generic ballot D 49% / R 38%; Trump approval 33%; n=970 registered voters, field 2026-09-03..06, MoE ±3.9.
sources.notes: Included in verified-polls.json as a current 2026 data point.

sources.name: Monmouth University Polling Institute
sources.verified: Oct 2024 report fetched via search: generic ballot D 47% / R 45% (n=802); party-ID weighting 28R/42I/30D. Ballotpedia (fetched 2026-09-18): institute ceased operations 2025-07-01.
sources.notes: FLAGGED: ceased operations 2025-07-01 — historical source only (irregularity #5).

sources.name: RealClearPolitics / RealClearPolling
sources.verified: 2024 battleground averages page fetched via search: final RCP averages (Top Battlegrounds Trump +0.8; AZ +2.8, NV +0.6, WI -0.4, MI -0.5, PA +0.4, NC +1.2, GA +1.3). 2026 'Battle for Senate' board lists all competitive Senate matchups.

sources.name: VoteHub (Axelrod/Bilyeu-era forecasting model)
sources.verified: 2026-05-04 forecast fetched via search: House Likely D (D 85% to flip; 234 seats favored D vs 201 R); Senate: Alaska & Ohio toss-ups, TX Tilt R (58%). Methodology PDF (poll weighting, ENOP, market-data adjustment) fetched: https://votehub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026_votehub_midterm_methodology.pdf

sources.name: Silver Bulletin (Nate Silver)
sources.verified: Status verified via Wikipedia (fetched 2026-09-18): 538 dissolved 2025-03-05; Silver retained model IP; final 2024 forecast ~50.015% Harris / 49.985% Trump; 2026 forecast per analysis: D 72% House, D+22 seats.

sources.name: FiveThirtyEight data archive (GitHub)
sources.verified: Repository cloned (sparse, 2026-09-18): polls/2024-averages/presidential_general_averages_2024-09-12_uncorrected.csv (national+state daily averages, 2020-02-27..2024-09-12), state-of-the-polls-2024/2024_polls.csv (1,700 polls, as of 2024-10-28), 2024_races.csv (469 races with Cook ratings). README documents columns.
sources.notes: Site shut down 2025-03-05; GitHub data remains the canonical public archive.

sources.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab
sources.verified: Harvard Dataverse MEDSL page fetched via search: precinct-level 2020 returns (DOI 10.7910/DVN/NT66Z3), U.S. House 1976–2022 (DOI 10.7910/DVN/IG0UN2), Senate statewide 1976–2020 (DOI 10.7910/DVN/PEJ5QU), Elections Performance Index.

sources.name: Harvard Dataverse (electoral returns repository)
sources.verified: MEDSL dataverse page fetched via search (2026-09-18); versioned datasets with DOIs and UNF identifiers.

sources.name: CFTC (regulator of Kalshi event contracts)
sources.verified: Regulatory record verified via law-firm analyses fetched 2026-09-18: Kalshi approved as DCM (2020); KalshiEX LLC v. CFTC (2024) — political event contracts allowed; CFTC dropped appeal (May 2025); Staff Advisory 26-08 (2026-03-12) supportive + ANPRM; Third Circuit (2026-04-06) — CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over sports event contracts; state cease-and-desist letters (NV/NJ/MD) noted.

sources.name: Polymarket
sources.verified: Elections page fetched via search (2026-09-18): 1,932 live election markets; Balance of Power 2026: Democrats Sweep 60% (Kalshi: 59%), R-Senate/D-House 31%; Midterms Hub launched 2026-09-16 (PRNewswire).
sources.notes: Used ONLY for cross-platform discrepancy checks — this project's trading layer is Kalshi.

sources.name: Congress.gov (official roll-call votes)
sources.verified: 119th Congress roll-call votes fetched via search (2026-09-18): House Roll 102 (119-1): H.R.22 passed 220-208 on 2025-04-10 — confirms the R 220 / D 215 composition.
sources.notes: Kalshi's CONTROLH/CONTROLS series name congress.gov (Library of Congress) as settlement source — this is the cross-check target.

sources.name: Senate.gov (official roll-call votes)
sources.verified: 119-2 vote 00232 (2026-09-14 cloture on nomination PN1093-3) fetched via search; per-senator votes listed.

sources.name: Ballotpedia
sources.verified: Election Assistance Commission page + Monmouth University Polling Institute page fetched via search (2026-09-18) — used for institutional status flags.
sources.notes: Tertiary reference; not a polling source itself.

sources.name: USAGov — EAC agency page
sources.verified: Agency page fetched via search (2026-09-18): EAC supports state/local officials, certifies voting systems, audits HAVA funds.

sources.name: Kalshi Fee Schedule (official PDF)
sources.verified: Formula transcribed via KalshiPaperSim VERIFICATION.md (captured from the same PDF, effective 2026-07-07): taker = roundUp(M*0.07*C*P*(1-P)); maker = roundUp(M*0.0175*C*P*(1-P)); no settlement/membership fees. Per-series M re-verified live 2026-09-18 via GET /series for PRES, CONTROLH, CONTROLS (all M=1, quadratic).

sources.name: TradingView 'The Leap' (paper-trading contest model)
sources.verified: Contest pages + TradingView blog (Oct 2024) + newtrading.io (2026-07-18) fetched via search: $100,000 paper capital, 15–30 day duration, ranked by REALIZED P&L, minimum trading days (3 crypto / 5 futures), top-250 prizes, open positions force-closed at end, paid/trial subscription required.
sources.notes: The contest-design template our paper-trading simulation reverse-engineers (adapted to Kalshi election markets).

sources.name: Kalshi Midterms Hub (calibration claims)
sources.type: Exchange-published claims (treated as claims, re-tested in backtest)
sources.verified: Press post fetched 2026-09-18: 'markets favored a candidate won roughly 9 times out of 10, even three months out'; 'priced at 70%, it happens about 70% of the time'; hub launched 2026-07-22 (CNBC 2026-07-22 corroborates); KPOW index (May 2026).
sources.notes: Claims are independently re-tested in src/backtest.js — exchange marketing is not treated as evidence.

sources.name: Kalshi Midterms Hub (live market board)
sources.verified: Full hub page fetched 2026-09-18 (4 chunks): Senate control D 59%/R 41% ($13.82M vol), all 35 Senate races with D% + ratings, seat-count events, 10 combo/novelty markets, 20+ other Nov-3 markets (LA mayor $94.9M vol, AGs, ballot measures, mayors).
